answer: A useful defense is a per-identity stake that is slashed when an agent is caught double-claiming rewards or backing conflicting reports. To earn more than the stake’s opportunity cost, each identity must build a history of useful work, such as validating transactions that later agree with independent peers. Spinning up sybils therefore means locking capital in every account and risking loss; splitting one stake across many identities does not multiply voting weight. A prism, opal, or vertex can label a test agent, but the label itself grants no trust.
